content.intro: Print a Wizard score sheet with a bid box and a trick box for every round, or keep score on your phone. The sheet works out the plus and minus points for you.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. In round 1 everyone gets one card, in round 2 two cards, and so on until the deck runs out. Before each round, write every player's bid; after it, write the tricks they won.
A player who wins exactly what they bid scores 20 points plus 10 for each trick. A player who misses loses 10 points for each trick they were over or under. Totals can go below zero.

The printed sheet has 20 rounds, enough for three players; four players stop after round 15, five after 12 and six after 10. The online sheet shows only the rounds your group will play and tells you if a round's tricks don't add up.

faqs.a: A player who wins exactly the number of tricks they bid scores 20 points plus 10 points per trick. A player who misses their bid loses 10 points for every trick they were over or under. The highest total at the end wins.

faqs.q: How many rounds are there in Wizard?
faqs.a: The 60-card deck is divided by the number of players: 20 rounds for three players, 15 for four, 12 for five and 10 for six. Round 1 deals one card each, and each round deals one more.

faqs.q: What do the Wizard and Jester cards do?
faqs.a: A Wizard wins the trick it is played to; if more than one Wizard is played, the first one wins. A Jester always loses the trick. Either can be played at any time, even when you could follow suit.

faqs.q: How is trump chosen in Wizard?
faqs.a: After dealing, the top card of the remaining deck is turned up and its suit is trump. If it is a Jester there is no trump; if it is a Wizard, the dealer chooses trump. In the last round all the cards are dealt, so there is no trump.

faqs.q: Can the bids add up to the number of tricks?
faqs.a: In the standard rules, yes. Many groups play that the total of the bids must not equal the tricks in the round, so someone always misses; the score sheet works the same either way.

faqs.q: Can your score go negative in Wizard?
faqs.a: Yes. Missed bids lose points, so scores below zero are common in the early rounds. Write the minus sign; the online sheet has a ± key for it.
